summary: Unexpected p95/p99 latency bursts correlated with adaptive/continuous batching for embeddings route
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent, high p95/p99 latency spikes and request timeouts on embeddings route since 2026-03-09. Spikes manifest as 2-5s outliers on top of normal tail latencies and several client timeouts (504). Problem appears during traffic bursts and correlates with adaptive/continuous batching behavior on the Dedicated pool serving Acme Retail.

Impact: Several customer production endpoints experienced degraded responsiveness for ~6-8 hours across multiple bursts. Business impact: search index upserts and real-time personalization requests timed out; customer reported user-facing errors.

Environment: Dedicated capacity pool (dedi-acme-01) in us-east-1, serving open-embed-3-small and rwd-embed-v2. Traffic pattern: bursty writes during ETL windows and steady read traffic during day.

Observed timeline: 2026-03-09 02:10 UTC first spike observed; repeated bursts 03:30-04:15 and 11:40-12:05 UTC. Support ticket opened 2026-03-10 by Acme support contact.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use Acme's repro: concurrent embedding requests at 40 RPS with 512 token context and variable request sizes (avg 1.2KB payload).
2) Target the dedicated endpoint URL and route to model open-embed-3-small.
3) Observe p95/p99 in observability dashboard and API response times.
4) Reproduce during simulated ETL spike by ramping to 120 RPS for ~2 minutes.

Note: Reproduction is intermittent and requires the scheduler to be in adaptive batching mode (default on dedicated pools).
logs:
Sample log excerpts (sanitized):
[2026-03-09T02:11:05Z] scheduler: batch_coalesce_wait=28ms, batch_size=48, route=dedi-acme-01
[2026-03-09T02:11:05Z] runtime: kv_cache_miss=0.12, kv_cache_evictions=3, latency_p99=2548ms, latency_p95=812ms
[2026-03-09T02:11:06Z] api-gateway: timeout 504 for req_id=4f2a... customer_timeout=5000ms
[2026-03-09T03:31:10Z] scheduler: adaptive_window=120s, observed_qps=86, max_batch_wait_ms=50
[2026-03-09T03:31:11Z] runtime: queued_duration=420ms, exec_duration=65ms, latency_p99=3190ms

Full traces and request IDs available in the linked dashboards (see related_confluence_pages).
investigation_notes:
Initial hypotheses: (1) Adaptive/continuous batching is increasing queueing for some requests causing head-of-line amplification during bursty arrival patterns. (2) KV cache churn due to embedding payload variance results in extra compute and evictions, magnifying tail latency for some batches. (3) Scheduler's max_batch_wait_ms and coalescing heuristics may be mis-tuned for dedicated pool traffic mix.

Findings to date:
- Reproduced p95/p99 spikes in staging using Acme's traffic profile when adaptive batching enabled. Disabling continuous/adaptive batching removed observed p99 spikes under same load.
- Traces show queued_duration spikes (200-600ms) immediately before high tail latencies; execution time per token remains stable.
- KV cache metrics show modest eviction rates during bursts; not the dominant factor but contributing under worst-case payload variance.
- CPU/GPU utilization on nodes remains <70% during spikes; not a pure resource saturation.

Working hypothesis: The scheduler's batching window occasionally coalesces many in-flight short requests into a large batch that causes a few long-queued requests to hit timeout thresholds at the gateway. This is exacerbated by the dedicated pool's default adaptive parameters tuned for throughput rather than strict tail latency SLOs.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Marcus Nguyen (Support): Customer reports p95/p99 spikes and intermittent 504s. Attached sample request IDs and dashboard links. Requested SRE assistance to check scheduler behavior.

2026-03-10 - Daniel Kim (SRE): Confirmed pattern in metrics. Queued_duration correlated with p99. Suggested temporary mitigation: reduce max_batch_wait_ms to 10ms for the dedi-acme-01 pool and enable strict tail-sensitive mode.

2026-03-11 - Lena Ortiz (Platform Eng): Applied temporary config change to dedi-acme-01 (max_batch_wait_ms: 50->10, max_batch_size cap lowered from 128->64) at 2026-03-11T01:20 UTC. Observed immediate drop in p99 for the next 3 hours during a small traffic ramp.
Customer confirmed lower error rate in first sample window.

2026-03-11 - Aisha Patel (CS): Customer side testing during peak window showed improved success rate but still occasional 1-2s p99 blips. Customer requested permanent fix and a postmortem with concrete changes to scheduler defaults for dedicated pools.

2026-03-12 - Lena Ortiz (Platform Eng): Begin rollout of scheduler change to treat dedicated pools with tail-sensitive profile. PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1287. Running canary across 3 dedicated pools.
resolution:
Workaround applied: reduced max_batch_wait_ms and cap on batch size for Acme's dedicated pool; recommended customer-side client retry/backoff settings. Engineering plan: merge PR 1287 to add 'tail_sensitive' scheduling profile for dedicated customers and default to stricter batch windows for pools with latency SLOs.

Next steps:
- Complete canary (in progress) and monitor p95/p99 across all dedicated pools for 72 hours.
- Postmortem to be published after canary completes and changes are rolled to prod (target 2026-03-16).
- Follow-up action: add an automated detector that flags queues where queued_duration > 200ms for >1 minute and toggles tail-sensitive mode automatically for affected pools.
resolution_status: Mitigation in prod, fix under rollout (canary)
